newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower on weak fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower on weak fundamentals.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Tuesday after trading in tight ranges as jitters over weak fundamentals depressed sentiment, brokers said.
The composite index ended 2.24 points lower at a provisional 725.59.
"Narrow fluctuations are likely to continue for the time being in the absence of government boosting steps," said Roh Byung-keuk, a broker at Coryo Securities.
Brokers said morning buying of theme-backed small-cap shares, fuelled by expectations of fewer stock supplies in December, could not sustain in late trading.
This month's stock supplies, including rights and bonus issues, would fall to 270 billion won from 900 billion in November, according to securities houses.
Brokers said the government's proposal today to revise labour laws aimed at ending violent labour strife and improving industrial competitiveness had little impact on the market.
"But it will have a long-term effect," said Kim Choon-kwon, a broker at Daewoo Securities.
Sammi Steel fell 290 won to its daily limit of 3,410 on rumours that the company faced financial trouble. Company officials denied the speculation.
Losers outpaced gainers by 458 to 407 with 157 unchanged.
Blue chips were under selling pressure as loans for margin trading remained higher than customer deposits at securities houses.
Samsung Electronics fell 600 won to 59,500 and POSCO 800 won to 40,000.
"Any rallies this month are likely to exclude large shares," said Yoo Jae-kyong, a broker at Daishin Securities.
Volume totalled 27.01 million shares, compared with 23.47 million on Monday.
